reconcile.connective: Harmonizers either sum the seven (three past famine years plus the current one plus three more) or judge it a copyist's slip for three.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the difference at face value: the same prophet, in the same divine message, offers David seven years in Samuel and three in Chronicles.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many years of famine?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/famine.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many years of famine?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: for the reconciling of which let it be observed, that there had been three years of famine already on account of the sin of Saul, Sa2 21:1; and in the current year, through the rains not falling in the proper time, the land was barren and unfruitful … and then three years more now proposed made seven years …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill's explicit reconciliation of the seven-vs-three difference: three famine years already elapsed (Saul/Gibeonites), the current barren year, plus three more proposed = seven. The fullest statement of the arithmetic harmonization on the row.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Shall seven years of famine come unto thee—that is, in addition to the three that had been already, with the current year included (see on Ch1 21:11).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB attaches the harmonization directly to the 'seven years' wording: the seven counts the three already past plus the current year, cross-referencing Chronicles. The most concise on-tension statement of the arithmetic reading; distinct voice from Gill.

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Ch1 21:12, the number is three, not seven; and here the Septuagint has three, the same as in Chronicles: this is no doubt the true reading, the letter ז zain, Seven, being mistaken for ג gimel, Three. A mistake of this kind might be easily made from the similarity of the letters.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke runs the alternative harmonization: 'seven' is a scribal corruption of 'three' (zayin mistaken for gimel), with the LXX preserving the original 'three.' A distinct strategy from the arithmetic reading; full verbatim sentences ending on real source periods.

pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, reconciling the seven against the three by reckoning three famine years already elapsed plus the current year plus three more, and also noting Kennicott's copyist-error proposal.
